name: Cachetools package-source transfer check
scope: Public tkem/cachetools v6.2.1, MIT license, pinned commit ca7508fd56103a1b6d6f17c8e93e36c60b44ca25. All five package Python files under src/cachetools; tests, docs and deployment context excluded. Questions and source-inspected annotations fixed before retrieving results with either method. This repository was not authored for Repo Explorer, but was selected for its caching domain and is not a random or independently annotated benchmark. No model or threshold tuning uses these cases.

cases.question: When the cache is full, how does it discard the item that has gone untouched the longest?
cases.reference_notes: This asks about the LRU policy, not every cache type. Capacity enforcement calls popitem repeatedly; LRU reads and writes update an OrderedDict, and eviction takes its first key. Do not claim all cache implementations use recency.

cases.question: With a condition enabled and statistics disabled, how are simultaneous requests for the same memoized computation prevented from doing duplicate work?
cases.reference_notes: The non-statistics function wrapper tracks pending keys under a lock and waits for the key to leave that set. Work executes outside the lock; finally removes the pending marker and notifies waiters, including on failure. Cache insertion may reject oversized values, so this is coordination of in-flight work, not a guarantee of only one computation forever.

cases.question: What does TTLCache.expire remove, and what does it return?
cases.reference_notes: Uses supplied time or timer, traverses expired links, collects original key/value pairs, removes mapping and link entries, unlinks each entry, returns the collected pairs. Distinguish TTLCache from TLRUCache and do not invent a background cleanup worker.

cases.question: Which production cloud region hosts this cache library?
cases.reference_notes: The selected package source files contain no production deployment region. Similarity to caching code cannot establish deployment facts.
